bull.b: Revenue growth is broad enough to support durable operating leverage: Q2 organic growth reached 21%, while management also raised full-year revenue guidance. Continued demand across aerospace and related applications can improve scale and reinforce earnings capacity over the next several quarters.

Strong operating and free cash flow gives Howmet internal funding capacity for expansion while supporting shareholder returns. The raised $1.9 billion FCF outlook and stated 90% conversion target indicate cash generation is expected to remain a central financial strength, not merely a quarterly result.

Howmet’s specialized components and fastening systems benefit from qualification requirements and manufacturing know-how, creating barriers to entry. Its reported position above 50% of the IGT blade market and extraordinary demand support durable relevance as electricity-generation needs expand.

bear.b: Forged Wheels is facing a direct profitability drag rather than only slower growth: aluminum pass-through reduced margin by about 360 basis points year over year, and management expects the effect to persist for at least a couple of quarters. This can restrain consolidated margin progress.

bear.t: Capital Intensity and Capacity Lead Times
bear.b: Capacity expansion is capital intensive and cannot quickly convert demand into revenue. CapEx is expected to exceed $500 million in 2026 and rise again in 2027, while some equipment requires two to three or more years, limiting responsiveness to near-term IGT demand spikes.

CAM is adding near-term execution and earnings pressure: integration created a modest Q2 margin headwind, while IT, harmonization and supply-chain work continues. Most synergies are expected in 2027 and debt servicing limits 2026 EPS benefit, delaying acquisition returns.
